UAV bootcamp

Code-to-Flight

Students explored how a drone flies and then put that theory to work by writing and running missions in simulation.

Participants
150+

Understanding flight

The first session covered how lift is generated and how roll, pitch and yaw describe drone motion. Participants learned how frames, motors, electronic speed controllers and batteries fit into the aircraft, then discussed feedback loops and PID control.

Simulating a mission

The second session covered the roles of ArduPilot and MAVLink. Participants used the workshop repository to write waypoint missions and ran their simulations live. A drone flight exhibition closed the bootcamp.

IoT design competition

Connexion 2025

Teams proposed IoT solutions for real-world challenges in patient monitoring, EV charging, waste management, women’s safety, green corridors, irrigation, and crowd safety.

Registered teams
25
Shortlisted teams
14
Finalist teams
10

How the competition ran

  1. 1–30 November 2025

    Teams submitted a brief proposal defining their problem and proposed solution.

  2. 5–31 December 2025

    Shortlisted teams refined their designs and prototypes through feedback sessions.

  3. 10 January 2026

    Finalists presented and demonstrated their work at Prayukti Bhaban, Jadavpur University.

Judging and results

The panel evaluated originality, technical feasibility, system design and clarity of presentation.

  1. Syntax_Error_404Women’s safety
  2. Tech EnovatorsEV charging
  3. Byte Busters 2.0Waste management

Jointly organised by the IoT Applications Club and the IEEE CASS Student Branch Chapter at Jadavpur University.

Competition · Srijan 2026 · 9–10 April 2026

IoT Bidwars

The competition paired a timed electronics quiz with a component auction, a circuit build and a cloud-connected motion-sensing challenge.

Registered teams
≈116
Teams in the quiz
75
Shortlisted teams
21
Finalist teams
8

Competition rounds

  1. Preliminary quiz

    On 9 April, the online qualifier tested Boolean logic, mathematical reasoning and electronics fundamentals.

  2. Bid-n-Build

    At Jadavpur University on 10 April, teams used a virtual ₹10,000 budget to bid for logic chips, then built a circuit using the parts they acquired.

  3. Uplink

    Finalists used an ESP32 and a PIR motion sensor to trigger an LED and buzzer, show readings on an LCD and send live data to the cloud. Three of the eight teams completed the full integration.

Results

Participants came from more than 25 institutions. Bid-n-Build and Uplink each counted for half the final score, with ₹15,000 in prizes.

  1. QBIT DynamicsHeritage Institute of Technology · ₹7,000
  2. Tech TitansKalyani Government Engineering College · ₹5,000
  3. Connecting the WorldJadavpur University · ₹3,000

Organised by the IoT Applications Club (IoTA) and the Department of Instrumentation & Electronics Engineering, Jadavpur University, in collaboration with the IEEE Circuits & Systems Society and the International Society of Automation.

Industry seminar · 28 February 2026

Automotive Electronics and AI

Ayan Bhattacharya, an R&D engineer at Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India (MBRDI), Bangalore, spoke about automotive electronics and potential applications of AI in vehicles.

Seminar details

Jadavpur University’s Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering organised the one-day, in-person seminar under the RUSA 2.0 programme for seminar and conference support.
